title: Sailboats on the Seine at Petit-Gennevilliers
credit_line: Gift of Bruno and Sadie Adriani
web_text: Painted outdoors in the year of the first Impressionist group exhibition, this work depicts pleasure boats moored on the Seine at Petit-Gennevilliers, a suburb of Paris, where sailing was popularized from the mid-nineteenth century. The view seems to be from a position on the water, and it has been suggested that this canvas is the picture seen on the easel in Édouard Manet’s famous Monet Painting in His Studio Boat (1874, Munich, Neue Pinakothek).

exhibition_history_text:
California Palace of the Legion of Honor, January 19–March 17, 1974; Santa Barbara Museum of Art, March 23–May 5, 1974; Fine Arts Gallery of San Diego, May 18–June 30, 1974. “Claude Monet, Paintings in California Collections,” no. 2.

Art Institute of Chicago, March 15–May 11, 1975. “Paintings by Monet,” no. 37.

Portland, Joan Whitney Payson Gallery of Art, May 7–November 1, 1987. Permanent collection loan.

Washington, D.C., The Phillips Collection, September 21, 1996–February 9, 1997. “Impressionism on the Seine: A Celebration of Renoir’s ‘Luncheon of the Boating Party,” no. 25.

Stuttgart, Staatsgalerie Stuttgart, September 21, 2002–February 9, 2003. “Manet and the Impressionists,” pg. 77, no. 103.

Paris, Musée Marmottan Monet, October 10, 2008–February 1, 2009. “Regards et Vision: Claude Monet, Edgar Degas, Mary Cassatt, Camille Pissarro,” no.

Sydney, The Art Gallery of New South Wales, May 1–July 1, 2010. “Paths to Abstraction,” pg. 106.

San Francisco, Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco (Legion of Honor), June 1–October 13, 2013; Salem, Peabody Essex Museum, November 9, 2013–February 17, 2014. “Impressionists on the Water,” no. 107.

Tulsa, OK, Philbrook Museum of Art, June 29 – September 21, 2014; Houston, Museum of Fine Arts, September 10, 2014 – January 29, 2015. “Monet on the Seine: Impressions of a River,” no. 11 [only exhibited in Houston].
